sentences.text: The petitioner is the accused in S.C.No.326/2025 on the files of the First Additional Sessions (POCSO Act cases) Court, Thiruvananthapuram, which arose out of Crime No.108/2021 of Aryanad Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram.

entities.text: First Additional Sessions (POCSO Act cases) Court, Thiruvananthapuram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offence alleged against him is under Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short, 'IPC').

The prosecution case is that, on 27.09.2019,
28.09.2019 and 01.12.2020, the petitioner indulged in sexual intercourse with the de facto complainant by giving the false promise of marriage.

It is stated that the petitioner and the de facto complainant were in love, and that the petitioner resorted to the commission of the crime, taking advantage of the above love affair with the de facto complainant.
2. The case has been registered by Aryanad Police on the basis of the First Information Statement given by the de facto complainant.
After the completion of the investigation, the Sub Inspector of Police, Aryanad Police Station, laid the final report, alleging the commission of the aforesaid crime by the petitioner.

3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that the issue with the de facto complainant has been amicably settled, and that the de facto complainant has filed an affidavit stating that she has no 2025:KER:50246 objection in terminating the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the de facto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. It is apparent from the prosecution records that the sexual intercourse between the petitioner and the de facto complainant, was pursuant to the consent extended by the de facto complainant,
who believed the offer of the petitioner that he would marry her.

The statement of the de facto complainant would further disclose that the petitioner has not retracted from the above offer, but only requested for a further time of two years for the solemnization of the marriage.

It is not possible to conclude from the prosecution records that the petitioner was not having the intention to marry the de facto complainant at the time when both of them indulged in sexual relationship.
Nor could it be said that there existed the element of deception in obtaining the consent of the de facto complainant for sexual intercourse.
Thus, it is not possible to say that the consent extended by the de facto complainant was vitiated by any misconception of facts.
That apart, the affidavit filed by the de facto complainant would reveal that she had already married 2025:KER:50246 another man, and started living with him.
Thus, it is apparent from the facts and circumstances of the case that the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC, is not attracted.

That being so, the prayer in this petition Muhammed Shahad vs State Of Kerala on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11112662/
2 to quash the proceedings against the petitioner, has to be allowed.

Thiruvananthapuram, are hereby quashed.
